note: Two `n1` entries in one `nodes` map (spec 6.4). This file expects NO diagnostic, which is the point: last-wins is what every mainstream JSON parser does, the first node is gone before any VNX code runs, and a standard parser gives a reader no way to know it happened. An arc's pips are its interior points only (spec 3.3.2), and its ends are its nodes' positions, so no rule of this format compares a node against anything else in the document: whichever `n1` survives, the arc runs from it, and nothing downstream looks wrong. Every reader built on such a parser therefore reads the same document here, and none can see the loss. If a reader ever gains the ability to detect the duplicate, this file goes red and the limitation is revisited rather than outliving its cause.
cannot_detect: A duplicate object key is resolved by the JSON parser before the format's own rules see the document. Detecting it needs a parser that reports duplicates - which none of the five target languages offers by default - so this is documented rather than papered over. If a reader ever DOES detect it, this file goes red and the limitation gets revisited rather than quietly outliving its cause.
